THE HON'BLE SMT. JUSTICE LALITHA KANNEGANTI CRIMINAL REVISION CASE No.392 of 2020 ORDER:
Challenging the order dated 07.10.2020 in Crl.M.P.No.439 of 2020 passed by the XI Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Anakapalle in connection with Crime No.716 of 2019 of Anakapalle Town Police Station, dismissing the petition filed by the revision petitioner herein under Section 457 of Cr.P.C for grant of interim custody of his vehicle
, this criminal revision case has been filed.
2. Heard Sri R.Siva Sai Swarup, learned counsel for the petitioner and the Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of respondent-State.

3, Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the revision petition filed an application under Section 457 of Cr.P.C for grant of interim custody of his Eicher Pro vehicle bearing Registration No.MH13 CU 6971 and the same was dismissed.

Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the said vehicle was seized on 13.12.2019 while he was carrying tobacco products and basing on the same, the crime was registered for the offences punishable under Sections 307,
353, 270, 273, 328 r/w 34 of IPC and Section 59 (1) of Food Safety And Standards Act, 2006 (for short "FSS Act").
He further submits except Section 307 of IPC, all other sections charged against the revision petitioner were quashed.
In support of the same, learned counsel has placed before this Court the copies of orders in Crl.P.Nos.12 of 2020, 7799 of 2019 and 2820 of 2020.

Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the~vehicle is very much required to the iano seinem aHRORE crt petitioner and retaining the Same in the police station will not serve any purpose.
He relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in General Insurance Council Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh! | wherein it was held thus:

entities.text: General Insurance Council Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "14, In our considered opinion, the aforesaid information is required to be utilised and followed Scrupulously and has to be given Positively as and when asked for by the Insurer.

We also feel, it is necessary that in addition to the directions issued by this Court in Sunderbhai Ambalal Desai (supra) considering the "(A) Insurer may be permitted to move a separate application for release of the recovered vehicle as soon as it is informed of such recovery before the Jurisdictional Court.
Ordinarily, release shall be made within a period of 30 days from the date of the application.
The necessary photographs may be taken duly authenticated and certified, and a detailed panchanama may be prepared before such release.
(B) The photographs so taken may be used as secondary evidence during trial.

Hence,
physical production of the vehicle may be dispensed with.

(C) Insurer would submit an undertaking / guarantee to remit the proceeds from the Sale/auction of the vehicle conducted by the Insurance Company in the event that the Magistrate finally adjudicates that the rightful ownership of the vehicle does not vest with the insurer.
The undertaking / guarantee would be furnished at the time of release of the vehicle, pursuant to the application for release of the recovered vehicle.

4, Taking into consideration the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner and also in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court, the criminal revision case is allowed and the order passed by the learned xX] Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Anakapalle in Crl.M.P.No.439 of 2020 dated ne '2010 (0) SCJ Online(SC) 1495 07.10.2020 is set aside.

The vehicle i.e. Eicher Pro vehicle bearing Registration No.MH13 CU 6971 is ordered to be given interim custody to the petitioner on condition of his executing a bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only)
with one surety for a likesum to the satisfaction of XI Additional Metropolitan Magistrate,
Anakapalle.
As a sequel, all the pending miscellaneous applications are closed.
